title.narrative: Rajasthan Secondary Towns Development Sector Project

description.narrative: The project will support the Government of Rajasthan (GOR) in expanding access to improved water supply services for about 570,000 people and improved sanitation services for about 720,000 people in at least 14 secondary towns by drawing on experiences and lessons from three earlier projects funded by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) in Rajasthan. The project will finance climate-resilient and inclusive water supply and sanitation (WSS) infrastructure in Rajasthan's secondary towns, including heritage towns; empower local governments and strengthen their institutional capacity; and deepen sector reforms to ensure improved and sustainable service delivery in line with GOR's investment program.

Status of Implementation Progress: The project is currently in progress, aiming to achieve its objectives upon the completion of ongoing works.
Water Supply: So far 1,591 km of water supply pipes have been installed, exceeding the targeted 1,350 km. Furthermore, 80,447 household connections have been established.
Sanitation: So far 1,151 km of sewer pipes have been laid out of the targeted 1,300 km.
Institutional and human capacities strengthened: Orientation sessions have been conducted for ward councilors, ULB staff, and line departments, engaging a total of 750 participants. MOU has been executed with 14 Government Engineering Colleges and 13 Private Engineering Colleges for a women's internship program, with two batches already completed, totaling 56 participants.
Overall, the project has achieved approximately 75% physical progress, and it is anticipated that the desired outcomes will be attained by the targeted year 2028.
